passage:
Monday. Hansa wanted to be out playing before six, so she raced through her maths homework in twenty minutes and skipped the checking. Her friend Ujjwal shouted from downstairs, and she ran.

Thursday. The teacher handed the sheet back: seven answers marked wrong for silly slips, a sign copied the wrong way and a missing zero. Hansa stared at the red marks.

Saturday. Instead of going out first, Hansa redid the seven, which took an hour, longer than checking would have. Ujjwal waited outside and said, "You lost more time this way." She nodded. On Monday she set herself a ten-minute check after finishing homework.

qa.q: How many answers were marked wrong?
What was Hansa feeling when she stared at the red marks?
qa.a: Disappointed and annoyed with herself, seeing that the slips were avoidable.

qa.q: What change did Hansa make afterwards?
qa.a: Hansa set a ten-minute check after finishing homework, before going out.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal's remark suggest about how Ujjwal saw the rushed work?
qa.a: Ujjwal saw that the rushing cost more time than a quick check would have, and said so plainly but not unkindly.

grounding: Shows a teenager rushing homework to reach leisure, making careless errors and having to redo the work.

passage: Harsha, put that phone down a moment. I'm Disha, your Nani, and I am not going to lecture you. I'm going to tell you a story. When I was fifteen, the science fair poster was due on Friday, and a cousin's wedding party started that evening. I hurried: glued the pictures crooked, wrote the title in a rush and spelled it wrong. My teacher saw it and said, "This is not your best." She gave me until Monday to redo it. I sat up two nights, cutting and gluing again, and I missed the wedding dance I had hurried for. Doing it slowly on Thursday would have been quicker than doing it twice over the weekend.

qa.q: What did Disha get wrong on the poster title?
What was Disha feeling as she hurried through the poster?
qa.a: Eager and impatient to reach the wedding party, and not thinking about the mistakes.

qa.q: What turning point led Disha to redo the poster?
qa.a: The teacher said "This is not your best" and gave until Monday, so Disha redid it over two nights.

qa.q: How might the teacher have seen Disha's poster?
qa.a: As rushed and below what Disha could do, and worth a kind second chance.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling how hurrying to get to a party led to careless work that had to be redone.
